summary: Oxford Co., Maine 36-foot steel tower erected in 1926, dismantled and removed in 1950; no source describes the site today.

events.note: Erection of a 36-foot steel tower completed; reported September 21, 1926
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: the erection of the tower was reported in September 1926
a crew rebuilding the Saddleback tower completed a 36-foot steel tower on Deer Mountain in Oxford County
evidence.quote: The crew rebuilding the Saddleback tower had just completed the erection of a 36-foot steel tower on Deer Mountain in Oxford County.

evidence.supports: a 1935 Lewiston newspaper item gives the tower a height of 39 feet
the 39-foot Lewiston item is dated May 25, 1935
the tower was dismantled in 1950 and removed
evidence.quote: The tower was dismantled in 1950 and removed.

evidence.supports: the Lewiston Sun Journal list gives the tower as dismantled in 1950
evidence.quote: Deer Mountain, unorganized territory T4, R2, 1926, dismantled 1950

evidence.supports: the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as US 102, ME 28
the site was registered on September 15, 2008
the registration was nominated by Henry Isenberg
the register gives no coordinates for the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1926 erection was 36 feet, and the record keeps that as the built height. A 1935 Lewiston Daily Sun item gives 39 feet, and no other source read explains that figure.

sources.title: Maine fire towers: By the numbers

notes_for_editor: The 1926 build date and the 1935 height rest on newspaper items quoted through Forest Lookouts. The 1950 removal is confirmed by two sources. No description of the site today and no access information. The brief's height 11.0 m matches the 36-foot figure. Two WebSearch calls, one of which returned nothing on Deer Mountain, and about four page reads.
